title: Mercor maps AI benchmarks against US jobs and finds most hours uncovered
friendlyTitle: Most working hours are barely covered by AI tests
summary: Mercor mapped 29 public, agent-style benchmarks onto the US Department of Labor's task list and estimates that 90% of American working hours sit on tasks with little or no coverage. Only 208 of 923 occupations have a task matched to at least five benchmark prompts. Coverage is deepest in large, already AI-exposed fields such as software and finance.
friendlySummary: Mercor compared 29 AI tests with a US government list of job tasks. It estimates that 90% of American working hours are spent on tasks those tests barely cover. Only 208 of 923 job types have a task linked to at least five test prompts.
whyItMatters: A high score on coding or exam tests does not say how a model will do the rest of a workday. Mercor calls the map provisional: an incomplete benchmark list pushes the coverage number down, and an automated judge did the task matching.
friendlyWhyItMatters: A model that scores well on coding tests may still be untested on the rest of a job. Mercor says the result is early, and a missing test makes coverage look smaller.
